newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi pardons son's killer moment before execution.
newsitem.headline: Saudi pardons son's killer moment before execution.

text.p: A Saudi man pardoned his son's killer moments before an executioner was to behead him by the sword, al-Riyadh newspaper said on Tuesday.
The daily said Hassan al-Thayab saved the life of Yemeni national Salem bin Mubarak by forgiving him for stabbing his son Turki to death.

"As the executioner unsheathed his sword and raised it to chop off the murderer's head...(the) father raised his hand and shouted 'Allahu Akbar' (God is Greatest), demanding a cancellation of the sentence," the paper said.
Under Islamic sharia law enforced in the desert kingdom, the victim's family has the right to spare the killer or demand his execution.
Crowds gathered to watch the execution cheered and replied with shouts of "Allahu Akbar".
"The executioner cut off a wisp of the killer's hair and gave it to (Thayab's) father as a sign that the murderer had been reborn," the paper said.
Some 81 people have been beheaded this year in the conservative Islamic kingdom, which imposes the death penalty for convicted murderers, rapists and drug smugglers.
